summary: The new scorer has sound protections against missing-age and blank-initial traps, but its advertised replication gate checks only some baseline rows and can approve a table whose recall or middle-initial results no longer reproduce the paper. The FamilySearch comparison also remains vulnerable to selective Ancestry fallback and common-source validation, and the script is absent from the documented replication runner.

findings.title: The replication gate can pass when baseline recall or middle-initial results differ from the paper
findings.what_the_code_does: The file promises that the Ancestry and ML columns must reproduce the paper, but `bad` is set only for denominators, `ver`/`unv`/`con`, and added/removed categories. It never compares `recall_*` or `mi_rate_*` with paper values before printing `REPLICATION PASSED`, even though both are written to the output table.
findings.why_it_matters: A change in the truth-pair universe can alter false negatives and recall without altering verified-link counts, while a change in the initial fields can alter MI match rates without changing any checked category. The script would silently certify and write changed baseline results, undermining the stated comparability check.
findings.how_to_check: Temporarily compare the displayed `recall_full_ans`, `recall_full_true`, `mi_rate_full_ans`, and `mi_rate_full_true` values with the corresponding paper cells; alternatively alter only an `mi` input and observe that the gate still passes if the checked counts remain unchanged.
findings.suggested_fix: Add expected paper values and fail-closed comparisons for every Ancestry and ML row emitted by the table, especially recall and MI match rate, using an explicit rounding tolerance for displayed percentages.

findings.title: The documented replication workflow neither runs the new scorer nor preflights its inputs
findings.what_the_code_does: The new file directly reads five link files, two divided-file directories, a congruence file, and an MLP reference, then writes `MATCHING/results/fs_linkage_abe.tex`. The machine-A runner's input list omits these new dependencies and its script list contains no call to `score_fs_links.do`; the scorer's standalone bootstrap also hardcodes `D:/repos/fixing_transcription_errors/replication/config.do`.
findings.why_it_matters: Running the advertised replication entry point will not generate this table, and stale or missing FamilySearch inputs are outside the runner's preflight. An external replicator cannot reproduce the new result through the documented workflow.
findings.how_to_check: Run `rg -n "score_fs_links|fs_linkage_abe|link1930_1940_fs" replication`; then run the documented machine-A master and confirm that it does not create `MATCHING/results/fs_linkage_abe.tex`.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a machine-A stage that preflights all scorer inputs and invokes the scorer, register its output, and replace the hardcoded bootstrap with a documented configurable entry point.

findings.title: FamilySearch-name links are evaluated against a reference built from FamilySearch profile-to-census crosswalks
findings.what_the_code_does: The scorer calls `mlp_training1930_1940.dta` `true_links`, treats exact agreement with it as verified, and labels the output `Verified Correct` and `Recall`. The repository constructs that reference by joining 1930 and 1940 FamilySearch profile-to-census crosswalks.
findings.why_it_matters: If those crosswalks were formed using FamilySearch's census index or associated names, the FamilySearch-name method and its validation reference share a source. Its verified counts and recall could then be mechanically favored and would not establish independent linkage accuracy.
findings.how_to_check: Document how each profile-to-census crosswalk was created and whether FamilySearch census names or search hints entered that process. Repeat the comparison on independently hand-adjudicated links or a reference constructed without census-name evidence.
findings.suggested_fix: Describe these outcomes as agreement with the MLP/FamilySearch-derived reference unless independence is established, and add an independent validation or sensitivity sample before interpreting them as correctness or recall.

findings.title: The FamilySearch columns conflate transcription performance with selective Ancestry fallback
findings.what_the_code_does: Upstream code substitutes each FamilySearch field only when its cleaned value is nonempty and otherwise retains Ancestry. The scorer reports the share of linked pairs using at least one FamilySearch field, but evaluates the resulting record- and field-specific hybrid as a single FamilySearch column; it does not separate both-field FamilySearch, partial FamilySearch, and complete Ancestry-fallback cases.
findings.why_it_matters: FamilySearch availability is plausibly related to legibility, name rarity, and linkability. Differences across columns therefore mix transcription-source effects with selective coverage and fallback composition, so the table cannot isolate how FamilySearch transcriptions themselves affect linkage.
findings.how_to_check: For each census side, tabulate `fs_frst_used` by `fs_last_used` among eligible records and linked pairs. Recompute match rate and reference categories for both-fields-FamilySearch, partial-FamilySearch, and fallback observations, plus a balanced sample with usable FamilySearch fields on both sides.
findings.suggested_fix: Retain separate first- and last-name source indicators in the scoring data, report their joint coverage, and add a common-sample analysis restricted to records with the required FamilySearch fields in both censuses.

findings.title: The table labels an age-restricted denominator as all 1940 men
findings.what_the_code_does: The denominator is restricted with `keep if age >= 8 & !missing(age)`, but the generated panel heading says `All men in the 1940 census`. It actually describes males aged eight or older in the divided files.
findings.why_it_matters: Readers will infer a broader population and denominator than the code uses, especially because children under eight are systematically excluded rather than missing at random.
findings.how_to_check: Count observations before and after `keep if age >= 8 & !missing(age)` and compare the resulting universe with the panel heading.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the heading and table note to state `Males aged 8+ in the 1940 census` and explain why linkage eligibility begins at age eight.

verified_clean.item: Missing ages are excluded from the denominator.
verified_clean.evidence: The restriction explicitly combines `age >= 8` with `!missing(age)` at MATCHING/score_fs_links.do:85.

verified_clean.item: Blank middle initials are not counted as agreements.
verified_clean.evidence: The code requires both `mi1930 != ""` and `mi1940 != ""` before evaluating equality at MATCHING/score_fs_links.do:223-227.

verified_clean.item: Proposed link pairs are deduplicated before rates and truth classifications.
verified_clean.evidence: Every link file is reduced to its pair identifiers and deduplicated at MATCHING/score_fs_links.do:156-162.

verified_clean.item: Truth classification checks both people in a proposed pair.
verified_clean.evidence: The scorer merges on both `histid1940` and `histid1930` and classifies a pair as contradicted when either side has another reference partner at MATCHING/score_fs_links.do:198-205.

verified_clean.item: Partner switches are now reported separately from net additions and removals.
verified_clean.evidence: The code assigns `status="changed"`, calculates verification for both partners, and emits three separate changed-partner rows at MATCHING/score_fs_links.do:275-317 and MATCHING/score_fs_links.do:363-365.

verified_clean.item: FamilySearch coverage is no longer completely hidden.
verified_clean.evidence: The scorer retains `fs_used*`, computes link-level coverage by census year, and writes coverage rows at MATCHING/score_fs_links.do:152-160, MATCHING/score_fs_links.do:188-195, and MATCHING/score_fs_links.do:361-362.

verified_clean.item: The checked baseline categories fail closed rather than merely warning.
verified_clean.evidence: Mismatched denominators, link-quality categories, or transition categories set `bad`, and the script exits before writing the table at MATCHING/score_fs_links.do:169-172, MATCHING/score_fs_links.do:235-241, MATCHING/score_fs_links.do:327-340.

verified_clean.item: Untracked review-report and prompt artifacts contained no additional executable changes.
verified_clean.evidence: `git status --short` identified the executable change as MATCHING/score_fs_links.do; the remaining untracked paths were under review/reports/.

review_limits: No paper draft was supplied, so claims-vs-code could not be checked against manuscript prose or paper table notes; only claims and labels emitted by the changed code were reviewed.

The external census and linkage data were unavailable, and the Stata pipeline could not be run. Counts, coverage shares, merge outcomes, and agreement with the hardcoded paper values therefore could not be empirically verified.
No generated MATCHING/results/fs_linkage_abe.tex was present, so its rendered appearance could not be inspected.
The extent of common-source dependence in the FamilySearch-derived reference cannot be established from repository code alone; that identification concern is therefore marked likely.
The review was scoped to uncommitted changes. Existing construction and replication files were read only where necessary to trace the new scorer's inputs and semantics.
